summary: The discussion proposes a new Parquet logical type, WIRE, to store serialized wire-format messages (e.g., protobuf) while preserving the original bytes and enabling selective columnar shredding of queried fields. It aims to keep the message intact, allow predicate pushdown on selected fields, and avoid breaking older readers, with a prototype in review and no current OSS engine support. The results highlight that gains shrink when measured against highly optimized existing code and that adopting a new layout adds complexity to writers. The discussion centers on creating a higher‑level document that compares several numeric encodings—DELTA_BINARY_PACKED, PFOR, FastLanes, and potential optimizations—across speed, storage efficiency, and development effort.
